messages:
rhea: heads-up: canary rollout of kernel-selector v2.5 shows a host-side tail increase for short requests. ingress p99 jumped 37ms -> 69ms and sys CPU +17%. spike aligns with short-request bursts.
dave: i pulled traces and socket stats. seeing a dramatic rise in writev syscalls coming out of the proxy/tokenizer. looks like many tiny http2 DATA frames are being flushed individually.
sandra: kvcache dashboard also shows higher async write queue depth and a few hot-shard evictions around the same timestamps. tiny fragments appear to amplify index churn.
 rhea: sanitized prod snippet:
```
[ingress] accept stream id=987
tokenizer: emit 64B chunk
proxy: writev([hdr,64,ctl]) -> flush
kernel: sys_writev x3 -> returns
```
 rhea: older behavior coalesced at ~1KB; v2.5's kernel choice tightened batching tolerance and now we scatter.
tomas: flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/3589990001 shows hotpath tokenize->proxy->writev->epoll loop.
bench-bot: nightly perf diff uploaded: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/10111/diffs/3589990001 (regression flagged).
dave: short-term mitigation idea: flip runtime `ingress.coalesce_bytes=1024` on canary hosts so proxy accumulates small writes until >=1KB before syscall. avoids adding ms windows but still reduces syscall count.
sandra: alternative: `ingress.coalesce_window_ms=6` (time-based) or `tokenizer.min_emit_bytes=128` (emit larger slices). each has tradeoffs: byte threshold avoids added latency when requests are large but may hold tiny streams longer; window adds bounded latency but simpler.
rhea: lab results: `coalesce_bytes=1024` -> writev calls -68%, ingress_p99 back to ~41ms, sys CPU -13%, kvcache async queue -40%. `min_emit_bytes=128` helps too but increases tokenizer CPU ~4%. numbers in PR.
tomas: plan: enable `ingress.coalesce_bytes=1024` on 10% canary at 3589990040, monitor ingress_p99, sys_cpu, kvcache.hot_evictions for 20m. rollback if p99 > 80ms or error% > 0.4%. i'll own the roll.
dave: long-term: add a `write_density` signal to kernel-selector. if per-host writev/s > threshold, prefer kernels that allow larger batching (or expose `batch_tolerance`). this avoids future regressions when kernels bias ultra-low-latency.
sandra: adding temporary alert: `kvcache.hot_evictions > 5/s` during canary window and `ingress.writev_count` delta > 50%.
rhea: i'll post rollback steps and perf dashboard links to #incidents when we start. thanks all.
